I am a final-year Computer Science and Engineering student interested in web development, software development, and space exploration.

For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I am interested in exploring how NASA's space missions and scientific data can be presented through interactive and engaging web experiences.

I am participating independently and looking forward to learning, experimenting, and developing a meaningful solution to the selected challenge.
summary:
**Forgotten Footprints** is an educational website developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge's theme, *Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars*.

The project explores four important missions through dedicated storytelling pages: ALSEP and Surveyor 3 on the Moon, and Sojourner and Opportunity on Mars. Each page introduces the equipment, explains its original purpose, highlights its scientific contributions and discoveries, and shares the story behind its mission.

Through an accessible website, informative content, and NASA images, Forgotten Footprints helps visitors understand that even after their missions end, these machines leave behind valuable scientific contributions and historical significance.

The project aims to make space exploration more engaging and understandable, especially for students and young space enthusiasts, while raising awareness of the forgotten hardware that helped expand our knowledge of the Moon and Mars.
details:
Project Details – Forgotten Footprints

Forgotten Footprints is an educational website developed to tell the stories of NASA's abandoned and retired equipment on the Moon and Mars. The main objective is to bring attention to space exploration hardware that is often overlooked after completing its missions.

How does it work?

The website presents four dedicated mission pages covering ALSEP and Surveyor 3 on the Moon, and Sojourner and Opportunity on Mars. Visitors can explore each mission to learn about the equipment, its original purpose, important discoveries, scientific contributions, and what happened after its mission ended.

The information is organized into a visual storytelling experience, supported by images and explanations that help visitors understand the history and importance of these missions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes space exploration history more accessible and interesting, particularly for students and people interested in astronomy and space science. It helps visitors understand that even equipment that is no longer operational can continue to have historical and scientific significance. My aim is to create awareness of these forgotten machines and highlight their contributions to our understanding of the Moon and Mars.

Tools and Technologies Used

I developed the website using:

  • HTML5: To structure the website and its content.
  • CSS3: To design the layout, styling, and visual presentation.
  • JavaScript: To add interactive elements and improve the user experience.
  • GitHub: For source code management and project hosting.
  • NASA resources and images: For researching and presenting mission-related information.

Creativity and Considerations

The creative aspect of my project is presenting the stories of retired space equipment through a dedicated website rather than simply listing mission facts. I focused on making the content informative, visually engaging, and easy to explore.

During development, I considered the accuracy of historical information, the relevance of selected missions, ease of navigation, readability, visual presentation, and accessibility. I also aimed to keep the website simple and understandable for visitors without a technical background.

Through Forgotten Footprints, I want to remind people that although these machines may have stopped working, their contributions to space exploration should never be forgotten.
